[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Image Segmentation: Semantic vs. Instance"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Image segmentation is a core computer vision task that involves partitioning an image into multiple segments or regions, often to locate objects and boundaries. In machine learning, segmentation goes beyond simple image classification or object detection by providing pixel-level precision."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Semantic Segmentation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Semantic segmentation classifies every pixel in an image into a predefined category. It does not differentiate between separate instances of the same object class. For example, if an image contains three cars, semantic segmentation labels all pixels belonging to any car simply as "car"."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Goal: Label every pixel with a corresponding class category."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Object Distinction: Does not distinguish between different objects of the same class."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Common Architectures: FCN (Fully Convolutional Network), U-Net, DeepLab."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Instance Segmentation"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Instance segmentation takes semantic segmentation a step further. It detects and delineates each distinct object of interest, treating multiple objects of the same class as separate entities. Using the previous example, instance segmentation would label the three cars as "car 1", "car 2", and "car 3"."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Goal: Detect objects and delineate their exact pixel boundaries per instance."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Object Distinction: Separates individual instances of the same class."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Common Architectures: Mask R-CNN, YOLOact."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Semantic Segmentation with U-Net in PyTorch"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a simplified implementation of a basic convolutional block used in semantic segmentation models like U-Net."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class DoubleConv(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels):
        super(DoubleConv, self).__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Conv2d(out_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x)"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary and Key Takeaways"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choose semantic segmentation when you need to understand the scene composition (e.g., autonomous driving road mapping). Choose instance segmentation when individual object counts and boundaries matter (e.g., cell tracking in biology or counting items on a conveyor belt)."}]
